items.problem: Legacy Windows.ApplicationModel.Background code migrated 1:1 compiles and renders but is behaviourally dead: the Register button never changes Status because a packaged WinUI 3 app needs a windows.backgroundTasks manifest extension (and the OnBackgroundActivated activation entry differs). This capped every scenario at partial.
items.evidence: migration-score.json behavioral_note: 'Register/Unregister produced no visible Status change in WinUI 3'; Package.appxmanifest (copied migrate-as-is) declares no <Extensions>/windows.backgroundTasks (grep shows only Capabilities). SampleConfiguration.cs RegisterBackgroundTask -> builder.Register().
items.proposed_improvement: Sharpen the existing background-tasks section: (1) warn that legacy Windows.ApplicationModel.Background APIs COMPILE in WinAppSDK but silently no-op/throw at runtime unless wired; (2) give the concrete Application.OnBackgroundActivated -> BackgroundTaskRegistrationGroup.BackgroundActivated (in App ctor) transform; (3) state the windows.backgroundTasks <Extensions> manifest requirement needed to make in-process registration actually function; keep the 'or switch to WinAppSDK BackgroundTaskBuilder' recommendation.
items.generalizes: Any UWP app with system/time/application/maintenance-triggered or grouped background tasks hits the identical compiles-but-dead trap and the OnBackgroundActivated gap; the fix is the same across scenarios.
